Need to search first.I don't have any notes for you yet. My research tools stopped working before I could read a single source on Jeremiah 45.

Here's what happened:
- I tried to open Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. The tool wouldn't open them because I hadn't found the pages through a search first.
- When I then tried to run the searches (traditional commentaries on each verse, Spurgeon and others on "Seekest thou great things for thyself?" in v. 5, and the NET Bible notes), the tool said I had used up my calls for this turn. No results came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I read nothing, I've left everything out rather than fill the gaps from memory or give links I haven't checked.

If you ask again in a new message, I can run the searches and write the notes. I'd start with:
1. The traditional reading of each verse: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight, and Precept Austin.
2. Differences between Protestant traditions: mainly sermons on v. 5 from teachers like Spurgeon (spurgeon.org), Desiring God, Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu) and Lutheran sites.
3. Other views: NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, the debate over where this chapter sits in the book), plus New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA. Any discussion of v. 5 against prosperity teaching would only go in if the sites actually cover it.
